updates.summary: React 19.3.0 is a substantial minor release introducing major new APIs including ViewTransition, Fragment Refs, and a new browser() DOM API, along with extensive bug fixes across the core renderer, SSR, and Server Components. While labeled minor, the breadth of changes — spanning hundreds of PRs across nearly every React subsystem — warrants careful review before upgrading production applications. The transition rendering model has also changed (transitions now render independently rather than entangled), which could affect timing-sensitive UI behavior.
breakingChanges: Transitions now render independently instead of being entangled into a single render — applications relying on the previous entangled transition batching behavior may observe different rendering order or timing.
react-server-dom-webpack/*.unbundled entries have been moved to the private package react-server-dom-unbundled, which may break existing imports if you used those entry points.
StrictMode now double-invokes effects after Fast Refresh and during hydration, which could surface latent effect bugs in development.
ramifications: New ViewTransition and addTransitionType APIs are additive but involve significant internal scheduler changes that could affect existing animation or transition logic.
Fragment Refs is a new capability that changes how refs can be attached; existing ref patterns should continue to work but edge cases may surface.
The new browser() API and onBrowserBailout server option change the SSR/hydration contract for browser-only subtrees, potentially affecting SSR-heavy applications.
Trusted Types API integration is now enabled, which may cause issues in environments with strict Trusted Types policies if not already accounted for.
Numerous Suspense, context propagation, and useDeferredValue bug fixes may alter previously incorrect but relied-upon behavior in edge cases.
Activity component behavior fixes (portal hiding, metadata hoisting prevention, error containment) may change visible UI behavior in apps using Activity/Offscreen.
Fast Refresh now remounts more aggressively on certain component type changes, which could expose issues in development hot-reload workflows.
SSR abort handling has been significantly reworked with multiple fixes; apps using streaming SSR with aborts should be tested thoroughly.

updates.summary: React 19.3 is a significant minor release introducing major new features including ViewTransition animations, Fragment Refs, and a new browser() API for browser-only subtrees. While categorized as minor, the sheer volume of changes across the renderer, server components, and DOM layer — along with notable behavioral changes like independent transition rendering — warrants careful review before upgrading. Most changes are additive or bug fixes, but the transition rendering change and Trusted Types integration could affect existing application behavior.
breakingChanges: Transitions now render independently instead of being entangled into a single render — a slow transition no longer holds up unrelated ones, which may change observed rendering behavior and timing in existing apps.
Trusted Types API integration is now enabled, which could affect apps that rely on direct innerHTML manipulation or have Content Security Policies that conflict with Trusted Types.
react-server-dom-webpack/*.unbundled entrypoints have been moved to private react-server-dom-unbundled package, which may break imports in custom RSC setups relying on those paths.
StrictMode now double-invokes effects after Fast Refresh and during hydration, which may expose latent bugs in apps with non-idempotent effects.
ramifications: New <ViewTransition /> and addTransitionType APIs are additive but involve significant new rendering logic that could introduce edge-case regressions in animation or layout-sensitive UIs.
Fragment Refs is a large new feature with many PRs; attaching refs to Fragment nodes is a behavioral change in the component model that could interact unexpectedly with existing ref usage patterns.
The new browser() API and onBrowserBailout option change how server rendering handles browser-only subtrees, potentially affecting SSR/hydration behavior in Next.js or other frameworks.
Several context propagation bugs through Suspense boundaries have been fixed, which could change previously incorrect-but-stable behavior in apps relying on Suspense with context.
Fix for useDeferredValue getting stuck may alter render timing in apps that rely on deferred values for performance optimization.
Batching updates from resize events until the next frame could affect apps that depend on synchronous resize event handling.
Multiple SSR/RSC abort and streaming fixes could change error handling behavior in server-rendered applications.
defaultValue behavior for type='number' inputs has been updated to match other input types, which could affect controlled/uncontrolled form behavior.
Fast Refresh now remounts more aggressively in development, which may surface previously hidden bugs during development.
Performance is improved in several RSC payload parsing and serialization paths, which is generally safe but involves significant internal refactoring.

updates.summary: React 19.3.0 is a substantial minor release introducing major new APIs including ViewTransition, Fragment Refs, and a new browser() DOM API, along with extensive bug fixes across the core renderer, SSR, and Server Components. While labeled minor, the breadth of changes — spanning hundreds of PRs across nearly every React subsystem — warrants careful review before upgrading production applications. The transition rendering model has also changed (transitions now render independently rather than entangled), which could affect timing-sensitive UI behavior.
breakingChanges: Transitions now render independently instead of being entangled into a single render — applications relying on the previous entangled transition batching behavior may observe different rendering order or timing.
react-server-dom-webpack/*.unbundled entries have been moved to the private package react-server-dom-unbundled, which may break existing imports if you used those entry points.
StrictMode now double-invokes effects after Fast Refresh and during hydration, which could surface latent effect bugs in development.
ramifications: New ViewTransition and addTransitionType APIs are additive but involve significant internal scheduler changes that could affect existing animation or transition logic.
Fragment Refs is a new capability that changes how refs can be attached; existing ref patterns should continue to work but edge cases may surface.
The new browser() API and onBrowserBailout server option change the SSR/hydration contract for browser-only subtrees, potentially affecting SSR-heavy applications.
Trusted Types API integration is now enabled, which may cause issues in environments with strict Trusted Types policies if not already accounted for.
Numerous Suspense, context propagation, and useDeferredValue bug fixes may alter previously incorrect but relied-upon behavior in edge cases.
Activity component behavior fixes (portal hiding, metadata hoisting prevention, error containment) may change visible UI behavior in apps using Activity/Offscreen.
Fast Refresh now remounts more aggressively on certain component type changes, which could expose issues in development hot-reload workflows.
SSR abort handling has been significantly reworked with multiple fixes; apps using streaming SSR with aborts should be tested thoroughly.

updates.summary: React 19.3.0 is a substantial minor release introducing major new APIs including ViewTransition, Fragment Refs, and a new browser() DOM API, along with extensive bug fixes across the core renderer, SSR, and Server Components. While labeled minor, the breadth of changes — spanning hundreds of PRs across nearly every React subsystem — warrants careful review before upgrading production applications. The transition rendering model has also changed (transitions now render independently rather than entangled), which could affect timing-sensitive UI behavior.
breakingChanges: Transitions now render independently instead of being entangled into a single render — applications relying on the previous entangled transition batching behavior may observe different rendering order or timing.
react-server-dom-webpack/*.unbundled entries have been moved to the private package react-server-dom-unbundled, which may break existing imports if you used those entry points.
StrictMode now double-invokes effects after Fast Refresh and during hydration, which could surface latent effect bugs in development.
ramifications: New ViewTransition and addTransitionType APIs are additive but involve significant internal scheduler changes that could affect existing animation or transition logic.
Fragment Refs is a new capability that changes how refs can be attached; existing ref patterns should continue to work but edge cases may surface.
The new browser() API and onBrowserBailout server option change the SSR/hydration contract for browser-only subtrees, potentially affecting SSR-heavy applications.
Trusted Types API integration is now enabled, which may cause issues in environments with strict Trusted Types policies if not already accounted for.
Numerous Suspense, context propagation, and useDeferredValue bug fixes may alter previously incorrect but relied-upon behavior in edge cases.
Activity component behavior fixes (portal hiding, metadata hoisting prevention, error containment) may change visible UI behavior in apps using Activity/Offscreen.
Fast Refresh now remounts more aggressively on certain component type changes, which could expose issues in development hot-reload workflows.
SSR abort handling has been significantly reworked with multiple fixes; apps using streaming SSR with aborts should be tested thoroughly.

Fragment Refs is a new capability that changes how refs can be attached; existing ref patterns should continue to work but edge cases may surface.

The upgrade brings meaningful improvements but requires careful validation due to the large version gap and potential behavioral changes in locators and tracing.
breakingChanges: The experimental packages @playwright/experimental-ct-react, @playwright/experimental-ct-react17, and @playwright/experimental-ct-vue will no longer be updated — migration required if in use.
Ubuntu 20.04 is no longer supported as a platform.
frameLocator() called without a selector now searches any frame in the subtree, which may change behavior for existing tests relying on scoped frame resolution.
Browser versions have been substantially updated (Chromium 153, Firefox 155, WebKit 26.6), which may affect visual snapshot tests or browser-specific behavior.
ramifications: Existing visual regression snapshots may need to be regenerated due to major browser version bumps across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.

Linux arm64 CI environments will now download Chrome for Testing instead of a custom Chromium build, potentially affecting execution in those environments.
The --reporter CLI flag behavior is now differentiated from --add-reporter; any CI scripts using --reporter may behave differently if multiple reporters were expected to stack.
httpCredentials now accepts an array, which is backward compatible but warrants review if credential handling logic is customized.
Tracing configuration changes (snapshots now accept an object) may require updates to playwright.config.ts if custom tracing options were set.
The new perfetto reporter and HTML waterfall view are additive but may affect CI output parsing if reporters are tightly coupled to specific output formats.

updates.summary: React 19.3.0 is a substantial minor release introducing major new APIs including ViewTransition, Fragment Refs, and a new browser() DOM API, along with extensive bug fixes across the core renderer, SSR, and Server Components. While labeled minor, the breadth of changes — spanning hundreds of PRs across nearly every React subsystem — warrants careful review before upgrading production applications. The transition rendering model has also changed (transitions now render independently rather than entangled), which could affect timing-sensitive UI behavior.
breakingChanges: Transitions now render independently instead of being entangled into a single render — applications relying on the previous entangled transition batching behavior may observe different rendering order or timing.
react-server-dom-webpack/*.unbundled entries have been moved to the private package react-server-dom-unbundled, which may break existing imports if you used those entry points.
StrictMode now double-invokes effects after Fast Refresh and during hydration, which could surface latent effect bugs in development.
ramifications: New ViewTransition and addTransitionType APIs are additive but involve significant internal scheduler changes that could affect existing animation or transition logic.
Fragment Refs is a new capability that changes how refs can be attached; existing ref patterns should continue to work but edge cases may surface.
The new browser() API and onBrowserBailout server option change the SSR/hydration contract for browser-only subtrees, potentially affecting SSR-heavy applications.
Trusted Types API integration is now enabled, which may cause issues in environments with strict Trusted Types policies if not already accounted for.
Numerous Suspense, context propagation, and useDeferredValue bug fixes may alter previously incorrect but relied-upon behavior in edge cases.
Activity component behavior fixes (portal hiding, metadata hoisting prevention, error containment) may change visible UI behavior in apps using Activity/Offscreen.
Fast Refresh now remounts more aggressively on certain component type changes, which could expose issues in development hot-reload workflows.
SSR abort handling has been significantly reworked with multiple fixes; apps using streaming SSR with aborts should be tested thoroughly.

updates.summary: React 19.3.0 is a substantial minor release introducing major new APIs including ViewTransition, Fragment Refs, and a new browser() DOM API, along with extensive bug fixes across the core renderer, SSR, and Server Components. While labeled minor, the breadth of changes — spanning hundreds of PRs across nearly every React subsystem — warrants careful review before upgrading production applications. The transition rendering model has also changed (transitions now render independently rather than entangled), which could affect timing-sensitive UI behavior.
breakingChanges: Transitions now render independently instead of being entangled into a single render — applications relying on the previous entangled transition batching behavior may observe different rendering order or timing.
react-server-dom-webpack/*.unbundled entries have been moved to the private package react-server-dom-unbundled, which may break existing imports if you used those entry points.
StrictMode now double-invokes effects after Fast Refresh and during hydration, which could surface latent effect bugs in development.
ramifications: New ViewTransition and addTransitionType APIs are additive but involve significant internal scheduler changes that could affect existing animation or transition logic.
Fragment Refs is a new capability that changes how refs can be attached; existing ref patterns should continue to work but edge cases may surface.
The new browser() API and onBrowserBailout server option change the SSR/hydration contract for browser-only subtrees, potentially affecting SSR-heavy applications.
Trusted Types API integration is now enabled, which may cause issues in environments with strict Trusted Types policies if not already accounted for.
Numerous Suspense, context propagation, and useDeferredValue bug fixes may alter previously incorrect but relied-upon behavior in edge cases.
Activity component behavior fixes (portal hiding, metadata hoisting prevention, error containment) may change visible UI behavior in apps using Activity/Offscreen.
Fast Refresh now remounts more aggressively on certain component type changes, which could expose issues in development hot-reload workflows.
SSR abort handling has been significantly reworked with multiple fixes; apps using streaming SSR with aborts should be tested thoroughly.

updates.summary: React 19.3 is a significant minor release introducing major new features including ViewTransition animations, Fragment Refs, and a new browser() API for browser-only subtrees. While categorized as minor, the sheer volume of changes across the renderer, server components, and DOM layer — along with notable behavioral changes like independent transition rendering — warrants careful review before upgrading. Most changes are additive or bug fixes, but the transition rendering change and Trusted Types integration could affect existing application behavior.
breakingChanges: Transitions now render independently instead of being entangled into a single render — a slow transition no longer holds up unrelated ones, which may change observed rendering behavior and timing in existing apps.
Trusted Types API integration is now enabled, which could affect apps that rely on direct innerHTML manipulation or have Content Security Policies that conflict with Trusted Types.
react-server-dom-webpack/*.unbundled entrypoints have been moved to private react-server-dom-unbundled package, which may break imports in custom RSC setups relying on those paths.
StrictMode now double-invokes effects after Fast Refresh and during hydration, which may expose latent bugs in apps with non-idempotent effects.
ramifications: New <ViewTransition /> and addTransitionType APIs are additive but involve significant new rendering logic that could introduce edge-case regressions in animation or layout-sensitive UIs.
Fragment Refs is a large new feature with many PRs; attaching refs to Fragment nodes is a behavioral change in the component model that could interact unexpectedly with existing ref usage patterns.
The new browser() API and onBrowserBailout option change how server rendering handles browser-only subtrees, potentially affecting SSR/hydration behavior in Next.js or other frameworks.
Several context propagation bugs through Suspense boundaries have been fixed, which could change previously incorrect-but-stable behavior in apps relying on Suspense with context.
Fix for useDeferredValue getting stuck may alter render timing in apps that rely on deferred values for performance optimization.
Batching updates from resize events until the next frame could affect apps that depend on synchronous resize event handling.
Multiple SSR/RSC abort and streaming fixes could change error handling behavior in server-rendered applications.
defaultValue behavior for type='number' inputs has been updated to match other input types, which could affect controlled/uncontrolled form behavior.
Fast Refresh now remounts more aggressively in development, which may surface previously hidden bugs during development.
Performance is improved in several RSC payload parsing and serialization paths, which is generally safe but involves significant internal refactoring.

updates.summary: This minor release includes one new feature for service worker header handling and four bug fixes addressing edge cases in middleware, server actions, blob key consistency, and URL preservation. The bug fixes address real runtime issues including a crash on oversized server action requests and non-ASCII blob key inconsistencies. The changes are broadly beneficial and the risk is low for most applications.
ramifications: New _next/static/service-worker/* header handling may affect sites using Next.js service workers — should be verified if your app uses PWA features.
The fix for 'preserve initURL' could subtly change routing or redirect behavior if your middleware relies on the initial request URL.
The await fix for Node middleware in edge handler templates could change execution timing in edge middleware; apps with complex edge middleware should be tested.
Non-ASCII blob key normalization between build and runtime may affect sites that serve content with non-ASCII paths or filenames — a re-deploy may alter cache keys.

Server actions that previously returned a crash response on body size limit will now handle the error gracefully, which is a behavioral improvement but warrants testing if you rely on that error path.

updates.summary: This minor update to ESLint includes several bug fixes, small feature enhancements to existing rules, and a performance improvement via fast paths in critical areas. The changes are low-risk and primarily tighten rule behavior (e.g., `new-cap`, `object-shorthand`, `no-unsafe-finally`) and fix edge cases. No breaking changes are indicated, though some rule behavior changes may produce new lint warnings in codebases that previously passed.
ramifications: The `new-cap` rule now only exempts built-ins that reference the global scope, which may cause previously passing code to generate new lint errors if custom globals share names with built-ins.
The `no-unsafe-finally` rule now reports unsafe labeled `continue` statements, potentially introducing new lint errors in codebases that use labeled loops inside finally blocks.
The `object-shorthand` rule now handles quoted properties for `ignoreConstructors`, which may subtly change linting behavior for constructor-related patterns.
Performance improvements via fast paths should have a positive impact on linting speed with no behavioral regressions expected.
The `prefer-object-spread` and `object-shorthand` rules now properly ignore `__proto__` properties, reducing false positives in edge cases.

updates.summary: TypeScript 7.0 is a major release that represents a significant architectural shift, as evidenced by the migration to the typescript-go repository (a Go-based rewrite of the TypeScript compiler). This upgrade carries substantial risk due to potential breaking changes in compiler behavior, type checking semantics, and tooling compatibility. Thorough testing of the entire codebase and all dependent tooling (build pipelines, linters, editors, type-check scripts) is strongly recommended before adopting this version.
